deals.headline: Levien entity buys out Erick Thohir; Stephen Kaplan joins as co-chairman
deals.investor: Entity controlled by Jason Levien, joined by Stephen Kaplan and new co-owners
deals.summary: An entity controlled by co-chairman and CEO Jason Levien completed the acquisition of Erick Thohir's ownership interest; Levien made an additional investment and was joined by incoming co-chairman Stephen Kaplan and new co-owners Al Tylis, Ed Shapiro, Robert Hernreich, Romie Chaudhari and Daniel Gilbert. Terms were not disclosed.

deals.headline: NFL running back Mark Ingram II joins D.C. United's ownership group
deals.summary: Ingram invested as a minority owner, pending MLS approval; terms not disclosed. Sportico later reported that the 2021 investments by Ingram, Yo Gotti and others valued the club at $710 million.

deals.evidence: the club expanded their ownership group with the introduction of four new owners
deals.headline: D.C. United add four owners, headlined by Yo Gotti
deals.investor: Yo Gotti, Adam Gerry (Granite Associates, Inc.), Jake Silverstein and Joe Mamo
deals.summary: Four new minority owners: musician and record executive Mario 'Yo Gotti' Mims; Adam Gerry, chairman and CEO of Granite Associates, Inc., an investment entity controlled by the Gerry family; Jake Silverstein, co-owner of Swansea City and former Houston Dynamo co-owner; and Washington businessman Joe Mamo (Capitol Petroleum Group). Terms not disclosed.

deals.date_text: Reported 27 September 2022 as in its final stages
deals.evidence: at an enterprise value of slightly more than $800 million
deals.headline: D.C. United sells up to 5% at an enterprise value of just over $800 million
deals.summary: Sportico reported D.C. United was bringing on several new investors for up to 5% of the club and its related businesses (stadium, training facility, sports betting operation, real estate development) at an enterprise value of slightly more than $800 million, including about $150 million of debt; proceeds were aimed at real estate development and capital projects at Audi Field and Segra Field. Investors not named.

deals.date_text: July 2026 (bill introduced; public hearing expected in the fall)
deals.headline: D.C. Council chair proposes $620 million Audi Field roof and expansion with $300 million of District money
deals.summary: Proposed, not enacted: Council Chairman Phil Mendelson's bill would create a public-private partnership with the club for a $620 million roof, 8,000-seat expansion and year-round facilities; the District would commit $300 million from its capital budget in $60 million installments over five years and the club would pay $360 million plus any overruns. It also covers housing on club-owned land next to the stadium.

deals.headline: Venture firm Collaborative Fund takes a stake in D.C. United and Audi Field
deals.summary: New York venture capital firm Collaborative Fund (about $1 billion under management) is investing in the club and its stadium out of its early-stage fund, the same one it uses for seed and Series A rounds; size and price not disclosed.

name: D.C. United
notes: Founded year left blank: the club calls itself 'One of the founding clubs of Major League Soccer in 1996' (its first season) and no page read states the year the club itself was formed. US clubs publish no accounts: revenue and operating income are Forbes estimates for the 2025 season (operating income is EBITDA as Forbes defines it), cited from the Wayback Machine copy because forbes.com refuses automated fetches; forbes.com/teams/dc-united still shows the May 2025 world-list entry. Sportico (2022) put debt at roughly $150 million, a gross figure, so net debt is left blank. No owner percentages are published. Kaplan chairs Nalpak Capital, his family office, and Silverstein chairs Stormlight Ventures (his family's investment platform) and co-founded Enfield Investment Partners, a sports investment firm launched in 2025 with an anchor partnership from PIF's SURJ; no page says their D.C. United stakes are held through those vehicles. Joe Mamo (2021), Al Tylis and Daniel Gilbert (2018) no longer appear on the club's ownership page. Leads not readable: a June 2022 Washington Business Journal report of Devin Talbott's stake and a June 2017 report of $120 million in bank loans for stadium costs (bizjournals.com blocks automated fetches). Danita Johnson is President of Business Operations. Not found: legal entity, average attendance, wages, social follower counts with a stated date.

The club lists fifteen owners, among them Mark Ingram II, Yo Gotti, Adam Gerry (Granite Associates, a Gerry family investment entity), Romie Chaudhari, Jake Silverstein and Devin Talbott; venture firm Collaborative Fund took a stake in the club and Audi Field in September 2026. No percentages are disclosed.
